sanskrit: yadi gādhānāṃ yadi nāvyānāṃ nadīnāṃ pāre nṛpatiḥ sakhā naḥ | viśve devāso abhi rakṣatainaṃ yathā jīvo vidatham āvadāsi ||
english: Whether on the fordable or the navigable side of the rivers our lord and ally abides — may all the gods protect him, so that he, living, may speak in the assembly.

sanskrit: yady avāre yadi vā gha pāre yadi dhanvani nṛpatiḥ sakhā naḥ | (…) ||
english: Whether on the hither bank or indeed on the yonder bank, or on the desert plain, our lord and ally abides — [may all the gods protect him, so that he, living, may speak in the assembly].

sanskrit: yadi yatsu yadi dhṛtyāṃ yadi samityāṃ nṛpatiḥ sakhā naḥ | (…) ||
english: Whether in the contest, whether in the endurance-trial, whether in the assembly our lord and ally abides — [may all the gods protect him, so that he, living, may speak in the assembly].

sanskrit: adhas padyantām adhare bhavantu ye naḥ sūriṃ maghavānaṃ pṛtanyān | viśve devāso abhi rakṣatainaṃ yathā jīvo vidatham āvadāsi ||
english: May they fall down, may they become inferior, those who battle against our patron, the munificent lord — may all the gods protect him, so that he, living, may speak in the assembly.

sanskrit: yama mṛtyo mainaṃ hiṃsīr yam ahaṃ hṛdā manasā jugopa | yo māṃ piparti yam ahaṃ piparmi sa prajāvān maghavān sūrir astu ||
english: O Yama, O Death, do not harm him whom I have guarded with heart and mind — he who carries me across and whom I carry across, may he be rich in offspring, munificent, a lord.

sanskrit: imāṃ nāvam ā rohata- -acchidrāṃ pārayiṣṇvam | narāśaṃsasya yā gṛhe śatāritrā bhagasya ca ||
english: Board this ship, the one without breach, the one capable of ferrying across — she who stands in the house of Narāśaṃsa and of Bhaga, furnished with a hundred oars.

sanskrit: upa dhuva gulgulunā- -ayakṣmāḥ santv aghnyāḥ | rudrasyeṣvā yātudhānān atho rājño bhavasya ca ||
english: Fumigate with bdellium — may the kine be free of consumption and unharmed; with the arrows of Rudra strike down the sorcerers, and those of King Bhava as well.

sanskrit: rudrāv īśāte dvipadāṃ catuṣpadāṃ tayor vayam adhivāke syāma | pakvair vitthaiḥ pratibhūṣanta enau vayaṃ devānāṃ sumatau syāma ||
english: The two Rudras hold sway over bipeds and quadrupeds — may we stand under their patronage. Let them be honoured with ripe viṭṭha-grains; may we be in the good favour of the gods.

sanskrit: pratīcī nāma te mātā śatavāro gha te pitā | tato ha jajñiṣe tvam ariṣyanty arundhati ||
english: Pratīcī is your mother's name; Śatavāra indeed is your father's name. From them were you born, O Arundhatī, causing no harm.

sanskrit: mātā nāmāsi mātṛto amṛtasyeva vā asi | arundhati tvaṃ sarvam abhi jīvam adhā idam ||
english: You are named 'Mother' from your very nature as mother; you are as it were the very essence of immortality. O Arundhatī, you encompass all life — and this too.

sanskrit: ā no agne sumatiṃ sambhalo ged imāṃ kumārīṃ saha no bhagena | juṣṭā vareṣu samaneṣu valgur oṣaṃ patyā bhavatu saṃbhageyam ||
english: O Agni, may propitious thought come to Śambhala; bring this maiden together with our portion. Pleasing in the choice assemblies, fair of speech — may she soon become united in fortune with a husband.

sanskrit: iyam agne nārī patiṃ videṣṭa somo hi rājā subhagāṃ kṛṇotu | suvānā putrān mahiṣī bhavāti gatvā patiṃ subhagā vi rājāt ||
english: O Agni, this woman seeks a husband; may King Soma make her well-favoured. Bearing sons, may she become a queen; having gone to a husband, may she, the fortunate one, reign resplendent.

sanskrit: somajuṣṭo brahmajuṣṭo aryamṇā saṃbhṛto bhagaḥ | dhātur devasya satyena kṛṇomi pativedanam ||
english: Fortune, cherished by Soma, cherished by Brahman, assembled by Aryaman — by the truth of the god Dhātṛ̥ I bring about the finding of a husband.

sanskrit: yathākharo maghavaṃś cārur eṣa priyo mṛgāṇāṃ suṣadā babhūva | eveyaṃ juṣṭā bhagasyāstu saṃpriyā patyāvirādhayantī ||
english: Just as the donkey, this fair and munificent one, has become beloved of the does, pleasant of abode — so may this one, cherished and mutual-beloved, be of Bhaga, pleasing her husband without obstruction.

sanskrit: bhagasya nāvam ā roha pūrṇām anupadasvatīm | tayopa pra yāhi taṃ yaḥ patiḥ pratikāmyaḥ ||
english: Board the ship of Bhaga, the full one, the one that moves without stumbling; sail forth by her to the husband who is to be desired in return.

sanskrit: idaṃ hiraṇyaṃ gulgulv ayam aukṣo atho bhagaḥ | ete patibhyas tvām aduḥ pratikāmāya vettave ||
english: This gold, this bdellium, this bull-offering, and this Bhaga — these they have given you for your husbands, for the knowing of one who is desired in return.
